scenario: [LERR.1.4.12]: a pair an operation ends records nothing, and a retraction evaluates no join test ([IRET.7.7]). `div_where` joins every Sensor against the nil token with `s.a / s.b > 1.0` (an all-Int division [LEXP.7.15.1]); `no_div` blocks `Tick` on the same test. Asserting a Sensor with `b = 0` and then a Tick derives one trapping pair at each node: two ComputationErrors. Superseding the Sensor with `b = 1` retracts the old one, which ENDS both pairs, and asserts the new one, whose pairs answer `2 / 1 > 1.0`, true, and trap nowhere. So the run records exactly two. PATH: libds's ds_rete_beta_right_retract on a positive node that never recorded a join returns without a scan (rete/beta.c); a runtime that re-tests the leaving Sensor records a third trap. Mercury drops the re-tests a retraction makes (ds.match.maybe_unblock). The runtime differential runs a larger form of the program (70_match_faults). `no_div` never fires: a trap keeps its block ([LNUL.4.7]) and the new Sensor blocks by a definite `true`. `div_where` fires once the Sensor divides.
rules_ds:
schema Tick scope logical:
    id: Int key

schema Sensor scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    state: Float? mutable
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable

rule no_div:
    Tick
    no Sensor s where s.a / s.b > 1.0
->
    log info "no_div fired"

rule div_where:
    Sensor s where s.a / s.b > 1.0
->
    log info "div_where fired"
